newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna to launch CECE derivatives on March 20.
newsitem.headline: Vienna to launch CECE derivatives on March 20.

text.p: Austrian futures and options exchange Oetob said on Monday it would start offering derivatives on its Central European Clearing House and Exchange (CECE) product line on March 20.
It will begin with futures and options on the Czech Traded Index, Hungarian Traded Index, Polish Traded Index and the CECE Index, which also includes Slovak shares.
"We want to offer quick and easy access to central and eastern European markets," Oetob product manager Guenther Schiendl told Reuters.
Market surveys had shown there was plenty of interest in this type of instrument and Schiendl forecast average daily turnover would reach 2,000 contracts by the end of this year.
"We hope that our investment will bear fruit soon...We are offering a platform for eastern european risk and want to attract international clients," he said.

Initially Austrian banks Creditanstalt-Bankverein, Bank Austria unit Investmentbank Austria, Raiffeisen Zentralbank and BAWAG would act as market makers. OeTOB was also hoping to win over German and French banks.
Schiendl said OeTOB was moving quickly to fill a gap in the market before east and central European stock exchanges came with their own derivative lines.
Schiendl said Oetob planned to extend the new product to the Slovak Traded Index. Russia, Slovenia and Croatia also figured on the exchange's mid-term agenda.
